neighbours.label: proper name of a historical ruler, figure or place in a historical narrative
fire: In 27 B.C., Octavian took the title Augustus and became the first Roman emperor.
Archduke Franz Ferdinand was shot in Sarajevo in the summer of 1914.
The emperor Hadrian ordered a long wall built across northern Britain.
Charlemagne was crowned emperor by Pope Leo III on Christmas Day in 800.
President John F. Kennedy was killed in Dallas in November 1963.
Cleopatra allied herself with Mark Antony against the forces of Rome.
The Habsburg emperor Charles V ruled lands in Spain, Germany and Italy.
Napoleon Bonaparte was finally defeated at Waterloo in June 1815.
quiet: In the first century, the new ruler took a grand title and became the first emperor.
An heir to the throne was shot in a crowded street in the summer of 1914.
The emperor ordered a long wall built across the northern frontier.
The king was crowned emperor by the pope on Christmas Day long ago.
The president was killed during a visit to a southern city in November 1963.
The queen allied herself with a Roman general against the forces of Rome.
The emperor ruled lands in several countries across western Europe.
The French emperor was finally defeated in a great battle in June 1815.
